Networking and Internet Architecture.summary: O-RAN enables a disaggregated baseband stack with programmable functions that communicate over standardized open interfaces. The same openness that enables multi-vendor composition also expands the attack surface across logically decoupled tiers that make up the compute continuum. Among these threats, Denial-of-Service and performance-degradation attacks, which account for the majority of catalogued O-RAN threats, are particularly difficult to detect. Traditional Time-Series Anomaly Detection (TSAD) methods fail in this new regime where labelled baselines are scarce, threats evolve faster than detectors can be retrained, and the high-dimensional multivariate telemetry overwhelms monolithic inference models. To address these challenges, we present DAST, a zero-shot multi-agent framework for cross-interface anomaly detection in O-RAN that chains a three-stage VLM $\rightarrow$ LLM $\rightarrow$ VLM pipeline. DAST converts multivariate KPI streams into visual representations, scores textual per-interface descriptions against O-RAN domain knowledge, and verifies suspects on high-resolution heatmaps to output the problematic interfaces, the anomalous time intervals, an indicative O-RAN WG11-aligned operational impact rating and the decision rationale. We evaluate DAST on real network traces collected from an O-RAN testbed under representative performance degradation scenarios, achieving 0.910 F1-Score and 0.843 Accuracy, outperforming state-of-the-art TSAD baselines.
Networking and Internet Architecture.comment: 7 pages, 5 figures. This work has been submitted to the IEEE for possible publication

Networking and Internet Architecture.title: An LLM-Driven Traffic-Control xApp for Dynamic 5G RAN Intents
Networking and Internet Architecture.summary: Programmable Radio Access Networks (RANs) enable runtime deployment of traffic-control functions, but selecting the appropriate configuration remains challenging as network conditions and service requirements change over time. Conventional solutions often rely on static rules or learning-based controllers with predefined state and action spaces, limiting their ability to accommodate changing intents. This paper introduces an LLM-driven xApp for traffic control in programmable RANs. The proposed architecture combines operator-defined service intents, runtime E2 interface telemetry, and the currently deployed configuration to generate traffic-management policies without blocking packet forwarding or the processing of incoming E2 measurements during LLM inference. Experiments on an OpenAirInterface 5G environment show that the proposed controller dynamically adapts the traffic-control pipeline to runtime intent changes, achieving an average intent satisfaction ratio of 0.91, compared with 0.52 for a static TC-RAN configuration. When channel conditions degrade, the controller maintains an intent satisfaction ratio of approx. 0.88, compared with approx. 0.4 for the static baseline.

Networking and Internet Architecture.title: Intent-Defined Radio: A Goal-Native Architecture for Next-Generation Wireless Networks
Networking and Internet Architecture.summary: Wireless systems are becoming harder to operate because service goals are increasingly expressed in outcome-oriented terms, while radio platforms still expose mainly low-level configurations and protocol-specific controls. This mismatch makes it difficult to translate latency, reliability, throughput, and continuity requirements into coherent radio behavior. This article argues for Intent-Defined Radio (IDR) as a new system abstraction for next-generation wireless networks. Rather than treating the radio stack as a fixed mechanism set to be manually engineered and then tuned, IDR connects explicit service goals to executable radio behavior within a constrained design space by leveraging the capacity of large language models (LLMs). We position IDR relative to programmable radio, intent-based networking, and learning-based protocol design. We also present two simulation studies using Intent2MAC to illustrate the design loop, demonstrating executable MAC synthesis and offline refinement guided by evaluation feedback. The results show improved service satisfaction at a throughput cost and improved remote-control performance when random contention is replaced by distributed urgency-based arbitration. We finally discuss the open challenges in intent specification, evidence, hardware execution, interoperability, and lifecycle cost, and outline a staged path toward deployment.

Networking and Internet Architecture.title: xAppGen: LLM-driven Natural Language Programming for Agile xApp Development
Networking and Internet Architecture.summary: Traditional RAN systems are closed and monolithic, stifling innovation. The openness and programmability enabled by Open Radio Access Network (O-RAN) are envisioned to revolutionize cellular networks with control-plane applications--xApps. The development of xApps (typically by third-party developers), however, remains time-consuming and cumbersome, often requiring months of manual coding and integration, which hinders the roll-out of new functionalities in practice. To lower the barrier of xApp development for both developers and network operators, we present xAppGen, the first LLM-driven natural language programming framework for agile xApps that automates the entire xApp development pipeline. In a nutshell, xAppGen turns high-level user intents into swiftly deployable xApps within minutes, eliminating the need for manual coding or testing. To this end, AutORAN builds a fully automated xApp generation pipeline, which integrates multiple functional modules (from user requirement elicitation, AI/ML function design and validation, to xApp synthesis and deployment). We design, implement, and comprehensively evaluate xAppGen on representative xApp tasks. Results show xAppGen-generated xApps can achieve similar or even better performance than the best known hand-crafted baselines. xAppGen drastically accelerates the xApp development cycle (from user intent elicitation to roll-out), streamlining O-RAN innovation.

Networking and Internet Architecture.title: SimPyWireless: A PHY-Aware Discrete-Event Simulation Framework for Wi-Fi and 5G NR-U Coexistence in the 5 GHz Band
Networking and Internet Architecture.summary: The growing demand from heterogeneous wireless applications with stringent QoS and QoE requirements is increasing pressure on available spectrum resources. Although mmWave and THz bands offer additional capacity, their propagation and hardware limitations make sub-6~GHz unlicensed spectrum, particularly the 5~GHz band, an attractive complementary resource. However, reproducible Wi-Fi/5G NR-U coexistence studies remain limited by the lack of lightweight, open-source, PHY-aware simulation platforms. We present SimPyWireless, a discrete-event simulation framework for Wi-Fi and 5G NR-U coexistence in the 5~GHz unlicensed band. The framework integrates shared-channel modeling, propagation, interference, SINR, heterogeneous traffic, mobility, and technology-specific channel access, while providing modular support for externally trained AI/ML models. We validate SimPyWireless against an analytical DTMC model and demonstrate expected coexistence behavior under varying contention and mobility conditions. SimPyWireless provides a reproducible and extensible middle ground between analytical modeling and hardware-based experimentation.

Neural and Evolutionary Computing.title: Synthetic Neurosymbolic Task Generation with Controlled Constraint Complexity
Neural and Evolutionary Computing.summary:
We introduce NeSySy, a synthetic generator for neurosymbolic learning tasks that jointly produces logical constraints and consistent datasets. Unlike existing benchmarks, NeSySy provides fine-grained control over key properties such as constraint structure, tightness, input dependence, and data generation and alignment strategies. In particular, it allows the use of rich constraints over infinite domains, and uses solvers to ensure that the constraints are meaningful and that generated samples satisfy the constraints.
  We design NeSySy to support both learning with declarative constraints and learning from distant supervision. Across a range of constraint families, we provide evidence that its parameters induce systematic and largely independent effects on task difficulty. Using NeSySy, we study constraint-aware learning methods, identifying regimes where explicit constraint enforcement is beneficial and where expressive unconstrained models can instead learn constraint structure directly from data. Our results establish NeSySy as a controlled testbed for analysing the interaction between learning and logical structure.
  NeSySy is built around a pipeline that incorporates solvers. Satisfiability checkers (CNFgen and Z3) generate and certify constraints. Constrained optimizers (RC2 for MaxSAT, Z3 for OMT) compute optimal repairs that guarantee every generated sample is consistent.

Neural and Evolutionary Computing.title: How to Effectively Manage the Energy in Residential Systems: Development and Comparison of Methods
Neural and Evolutionary Computing.summary:
The transition from fossil fuels presents significant challenges in energy management. To ensure a sustainable energy future, it is crucial to reduce energy consumption when possible and to synchronize electricity consumption and storage with the production from sources with low greenhouse gas emissions. This thesis explores a variety of energy management methods used to manage batteries, heat pumps, and other energy-related systems. The thesis presents three simulation cases alongside one real-world experiment to compare energy management done through simple rules, optimization, and machine learning methods. Furthermore, this thesis introduces TreeC, a novel machine learning-based method that learns understandable yet efficient energy management strategies, applicable to many cases.
  The three key contributions of this thesis can be summarized as follows: 1) The developed TreeC method demonstrates competitive performance compared to a variety of energy management approaches, such as model predictive control and reinforcement learning, across a diverse set of energy management problems. The understandability of TreeC's energy management strategies greatly improves the transparency and trustworthiness of machine learning-based energy management. 2) The real-world experiment highlights the need to validate energy management methods on actual hardware and not solely on simulations. Both TreeC and model predictive control performed worse than in simulations, due to, respectively, insufficiently representative training data and the real-time input data not being reliable enough. 3) Energy management algorithms reduce costs in electrified Belgian dwellings, particularly in poorly insulated dwellings, electric vehicle chargers, and photovoltaic installations. However, on average, these cost savings do not yet outweigh the current costs and effort required to implement such algorithms.

Neural and Evolutionary Computing.title: SpikingGamma: Temporally Precise Online SNN Training Through Smoothed Temporal Delays
Neural and Evolutionary Computing.summary: Neuromorphic hardware implementations of Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) promise energy-efficient, low-latency AI through sparse, event-driven computation. Yet, training SNNs under fine temporal discretization remains challenging, hindering low-latency responsiveness and the mapping of software-trained SNNs to efficient hardware. In current approaches, spiking neurons are modeled as self-recurrent units, embedded into recurrent networks to maintain state over time, and trained with BPTT or RTRL variants based on surrogate gradients. These methods scale poorly with temporal resolution, while online approximations exhibit instability for long sequences and tend to fail at capturing temporal patterns. To address these limitations, we develop SpikingGamma, an SNN architecture in which neurons maintain a compact bank of smoothed-delay states and communicate through sigma-delta spike-coding. We show that in feedforward networks, SpikingGamma supports direct online error backpropagation through the continuous reconstruction signal, avoiding surrogate gradients through the spike discontinuity. This enables stable learning of temporal patterns with minimal spiking and scales feedforward SNNs to complex tasks and benchmarks with competitive accuracy, all while remaining robust to the temporal resolution of the model. Our approach offers both an alternative to recurrent SNNs trained with surrogate gradients, and a novel route for mapping SNNs to neuromorphic hardware.
Neural and Evolutionary Computing.comment: Accepted at NeurIPS 2026

Neural and Evolutionary Computing.title: SCAR: State-Space Compression for AI-Based Radio Resource Management of Vehicular Services
Neural and Evolutionary Computing.summary: The increasing demand for connected vehicular services poses significant challenges for AI-based network and service management due to the high volume and rapid variability of network state information. Traditional management and control mechanisms struggle to scale when processing fine-grained metrics such as Channel Quality Indicators (CQIs) in dynamic vehicular environments. To address this challenge, we propose SCAR (State-Space Compression for AI-Based Radio Resource Management), an edge-assisted framework that abstracts high-dimensional CQI information into compact representations for AI-based management. SCAR employs machine-learning (ML)-based compression techniques, including clustering and radial basis function (RBF) networks, to reduce the dimensionality of CQI-derived state information while preserving essential features relevant to management decisions. The resulting compressed states are used to train reinforcement learning (RL)-based management policies that dynamically adapt the throughput-fairness trade-off according to service-level fairness objectives defined by the NGMN. Simulation results show that CQI compression improves average NGMN feasible-region occupancy from 56.32% to 88.07% across ten RL algorithms, reaching 97.76% for the best-performing RL configuration, with limited throughput degradation and competitive computational overhead. Furthermore, simulated annealing with stochastic tunneling (SAST)-based clustering reduces state compression distortion by approximately 10% compared with conventional K-means clustering. These results demonstrate SCAR's ability to provide compact state representations for RL-based network and service management while improving service-level fairness in dynamic vehicular systems.

Neural and Evolutionary Computing.title: A Matter of Representation: Evolving Partial Spreads for Bent Functions
Neural and Evolutionary Computing.summary: Partial spread ($\mathcal{PS}$) bent functions are Boolean functions of maximum nonlinearity built from families of subspaces that pairwise intersect only in the null vector. We design an Evolution Strategy (ES) to construct such partial spread families, comparing two encodings: one based on generator matrices of the subspaces, and one based on spread sets. With the latter, combined with a ruin-and-rebuild operator, the ES finds $\mathcal{PS}$ functions up to $n=10$ variables. An ablation study shows that mutation is necessary, while the population size is not, and that a restarted look-ahead greedy heuristic outperforms the ES on the hardest instance. We investigate this finding with a landscape analysis of the stagnation points, and we also introduce a quality-diversity variant of the ES which finds $\mathcal{PS}$ functions of low algebraic degree for 8 variables. Interestingly, the bent functions evolved by the ES have higher 2-ranks and mostly higher degrees than those obtained by a baseline Genetic Programming optimizer.
Neural and Evolutionary Computing.comment: 16 pages, 2 figures, 2 tables

Neural and Evolutionary Computing.title: The Price of an Explanation: What Demanding Verifiable Artifacts Costs, and What It Buys Back
Neural and Evolutionary Computing.summary: Generative models produce many candidate solutions but provide no intrinsic signal by which to rank them. One mitigation is to demand a \emph{verifiable artifact}: a program that can be executed against the available evidence. A common concern is that requiring executable verification incurs costs in both solution quality and computational budget. We measure these two costs on the $120$-task ARC-AGI-2 evaluation set. Demanding a verifiable artifact from an LLM reduced the score from $93$ to $68$ of $120$ tasks ($77\%$ to $57\%$). Of those $25$ tasks, $21$ were reached by no program-producing configuration we ran, at any budget, by sampling or by search; yet for $27$ of the $28$ tasks that only the answer-only arm solved, some program arm held a program that reproduced every demonstration and still failed the test. The bottleneck is obtaining an explanation that \emph{generalizes}, not finding one. A short evolutionary search over two already-sampled programs, at no additional model cost, beats best-of-$2$ sampled code by $9.2 \pm 1.4$ tasks, and over a single sampled program beats $1$-shot sampling by $9.9 \pm 1.3$. Moreover, because a program can be checked against the training examples, any program-producing protocol can terminate early once a task is explained: under the same stopping rule, best-of-$n$ sampling declines up to $38\%$ of its budget and the evolved arm up to $49\%$, whereas an answer-only baseline cannot terminate early. Applying the same methodology to decoder synthesis for quantum error correction yields interpretable decoders evaluated against a certified panel of published decoders on held-out exam shots.
Neural and Evolutionary Computing.comment: 8 main pages, 3 main figures. 19 pages total. Accepted in NeurIPS 2026 AI4Science Workshop

Neural and Evolutionary Computing.title: Arbitrary-Accuracy Neural Approximation with Optimal Neuron Count and Optimal Bit Complexity
Neural and Evolutionary Computing.summary: We study the minimum number of hidden neurons required for arbitrary-accuracy approximation of continuous functions on $[0,1]^d$ and the associated encoding complexity. For $d\geq 2$, we construct two fixed, explicitly defined activation functions and, for each, a closed-form network with two hidden layers of widths $d$ and $1$ that achieves arbitrary accuracy in the uniform norm. We prove that $d+1$ is the exact minimum total number of hidden neurons among standard feedforward networks with locally integrable activations and affine outputs. We further give a simpler construction using a single elementary activation that combines the floor and exponential functions. This construction requires three hidden layers of widths $d$, $1$, and $2$. If a skip connection is allowed, widths $d$, $1$, and $1$ suffice. For a bounded $α$-Hölder class with $α\in(0,1]$, the networks with the digit-extraction activation and with the elementary activation require $O(\varepsilon^{-d/α}\log(1/\varepsilon))$ bits, matching the metric-entropy lower bound up to a logarithmic factor. The other $(d,1)$ network, which stores differences of neighboring values along a spanning tree, needs only $Θ(\varepsilon^{-d/α})$ bits and is optimal in both neuron count and bit complexity.

Neural and Evolutionary Computing.title: Evolving Decoding Algorithms for Quantum Error Correction
Neural and Evolutionary Computing.summary: Quantum computation entails robustness engineering: a noisy quantum state is measured continuously, and a classical algorithm (the decoder) must infer corrections that reliably remove the noise, fast enough to keep up. We write several published belief-propagation (BP) decoders for quantum low-density parity-check (qLDPC) codes in a Domain-Specific Language (DSL), and search over it with grammatical evolution. Written in the language, the published decoders show their parameters in plain view, allowing us to re-parameterise BP+OSD (ordered statistics decoding) and BP+LSD (localized statistics decoding) decoders with damping, before any search, making each 17.1--41.0$\times$ faster at a higher error rate, and BP+OSD-0 about 103 faster than the ldpc package's version tuned on the [[72,12,6]] bivariate-bicycle code. Evolution over the language finds decoders that improve the time-error front. One makes 23% fewer logical errors than BP+OSD-0 with damping at 0.64$\times$ its time, and decoders evolved from random code are more accurate than ldpc's tuned BP+OSD-0 at 1/31 of its time or less. Frozen at one operating point, the two fastest evolved decoders generalize well across noise levels, code sizes and round counts, staying at the time-error front. Ultimately, we demonstrate that capturing expert knowledge within a DSL creates a powerful intermediate layer---one that effectively bridges human intuition and machine-driven optimization to unlock highly efficient quantum error correction.
Neural and Evolutionary Computing.comment: 5 main pages, 2 main figures. 15 total pages. Accepted in NeurIPS 2026 EvoRobust Workshop

Neural and Evolutionary Computing.title: Flex-Plorer: A Precision-Aware Hardware-Software Co-Design Framework for an Edge SNN Accelerator
Neural and Evolutionary Computing.summary: Neuromorphic accelerators promise high energy efficiency and computational density for spiking neural networks (SNNs), especially in wearable devices and neural prosthetics where power constraints are stringent. However, most existing platforms exhibit rigid architectures with limited configurability, which restricts their adaptability to heterogeneous signals and diverse design objectives. To address this gap, we present Flex-Plorer, a precision-aware hardware-software co-design framework using heuristic search over weight and decay precisions for a fixed architecture. It couples hardware-aware fixed-point simulation with synthesis-trained LUT/FF estimators and analytical BRAM estimation to guide user-defined accuracy-resource trade-offs without per-candidate synthesis. The best-found configuration generates specialized RTL, drivers, and deployment data. Its substrate, Flexi-NeurA, supports multiple neuron models and topologies through event-driven, time-multiplexed cores with shared neuron datapaths and address-event communication. Design-time component selection and automatic memory sizing specialize the implementation without manual RTL modification. Comprehensive evaluations demonstrate the versatility of the proposed flow across three application domains: (i) auditory processing, achieving 75% accuracy with an energy consumption of 1.48mJ per inference; (ii) dynamic vision sensor gesture recognition, achieving 93% accuracy at 0.55mJ; and (iii) standard vision classification, achieving 97% accuracy at 0.12mJ. Together, Flex-Plorer and Flexi-NeurA form an application-adaptive, energy-efficient co-design flow for deploying SNNs across heterogeneous edge-AI workloads.

Neural and Evolutionary Computing.title: HabitusMem: Belief Memory over Evolving User Preferences for LLM Agents
Neural and Evolutionary Computing.summary: Personalized LLM agents must act on a user's current preferences, which change across interactions and are rarely stated in full. Existing memory systems store and retrieve content from the interaction history and leave the agent to work out which preferences still hold and where they apply. Such content does not indicate whether a preference is still current or where it applies, so agents often act on outdated or misapplied preferences. We instead treat memory as the assistant's belief about the user. Following Bourdieu's account of habitus as durable but revisable dispositions, we model the user as a latent preference state that every interaction, including the current request, both reveals and updates. The belief summarizes what the history supports about this state, and memory consists of the individual beliefs that bear on the agent's current decision, each with its evidence, scope, and status. We implement this view in HabitusMem, a trained writer that states these beliefs as text records for a frozen agent. Across two agent families, HabitusMem achieves the best results among memory systems on both PersonaMem-v2 and VitaBench 2.0. Controlled analyses show that learned request conditioning drives the answering gain, while auxiliary training tasks improve tool use.

Neural and Evolutionary Computing.title: Sensorimotor behavior from an untrained brain-and-nerve-cord connectome
Neural and Evolutionary Computing.summary: Connectomes map the neurons and synapses of an adult fly's brain and nerve cord, but how much of behavior follows from the wiring is unknown. Here we turn one such connectome into a spiking network of 172,433 neurons with a published brain model's untuned parameters, and run it alone and inside a simulated body. Two fixed rules connect them: odors and looming objects set the firing of the sensory neurons, and the firing of the leg motor neurons moves the legs. Outside the body, a pathway of known function conducts when it supplies a few percent or more of its target's input. In the body, the fly navigates around obstacles to nearly every odor source. A rewiring that keeps each neuron's connection counts and signs reaches far fewer, and the fly's leg commands replayed with the senses off reach almost none. Navigation needs the measured wiring and sensory feedback. Dopamine-gated weakening of the mushroom body's output synapses turns approach to an odor into avoidance, and the learning is associative once one class of olfactory synapse is scaled. An untrained connectome supports a behavior and its learned reversal. The pathways it cannot drive show what the wiring diagram leaves out.

Neural and Evolutionary Computing.title: Hierarchical Spatiotemporal World Modeling with Content-Adaptive Spatial Addressing
Neural and Evolutionary Computing.summary: Long-horizon world modeling in partially observable environments requires compact memories that preserve spatial structure despite accumulated localization drift. Inspired by hippocampal episodic and spatial memory and the multi-periodic coding of entorhinal grid cells, we propose HiSTFormer, a hierarchical spatiotemporal world model, which adopts a layer-wise organization of local temporal RoPE and multi-periodic spatial RoPE, together with content-conditioned address offsets, to capture recent temporal context and long-range spatial structure. A fixed-capacity memory keeps KV storage and per-step attention cost bounded as the sequence grows. On MemoryMaze and HM3D, HiSTFormer outperforms strong world-model baselines within the training sequence length and generalizes substantially better to prediction horizons far beyond those seen during training, while using a compact model. The hierarchical spatiotemporal design remains effective across deeper Transformer stacks, with consistent gains as depth increases. These results show that hierarchical spatiotemporal organization and content-adaptive spatial addressing provide effective inductive biases for efficient long-horizon world modeling.

Neural and Evolutionary Computing.title: Compiling Constraints into Neuromorphic Ising Machines
Neural and Evolutionary Computing.summary: Most practical combinatorial optimization problems involve constraints, and an Ising machine that flips one spin at a time can respect them only through energy penalties that raise barriers between feasible solutions. Here we show that a higher-order neuromorphic Ising machine can enforce constraints through programmable transitions rather than penalties. In an autoencoder-like architecture, each inner-layer neuron represents a move, a family of multi-spin transitions that maps every feasible state to another feasible state, receives the energy change of its move through connections that outer-layer neurons multiplicatively switch on or off, and updates the state through the same connections. A compiler turns constraints into this wiring with a number of auxiliary clauses that grows only polynomially for parity, cardinality, one-hot, partition and permutation constraints. Restricting the search to feasible states reduces constraint handling to move design, and we show that the fastest-annealing moves are not those that mix fastest but those that lower the deepest energy barriers, and that moves chosen from the objective lower them further than random ones. On third-order graph matching, the machine needs orders of magnitude fewer iterations than penalty-based neuromorphic machines. Configured as a sampler on a field-programmable gate array, it decodes the surface code with maximum-likelihood accuracy up to code distance 15 within 52 $μ$s per shot and, under noisy syndrome measurements, decodes in real time for millisecond measurement rounds up to distance 9 with fewer logical errors than belief-propagation decoders.
Neural and Evolutionary Computing.comment: 41 pages, 6 figures, with Supplementary Information (46 pages)

Neural and Evolutionary Computing.title: Attention at Absolute Zero
Neural and Evolutionary Computing.summary: Attention scores candidate supports of an answer, which we call witnesses, and reads the scores at a temperature. We build a higher-order attention layer whose state lives on pairs of items: for a pair (a, b), each third item k is a witness judged through its legs (a, k) and (k, b). It reads witnesses at zero temperature, keeping the best and the number tied with it, passes on only bits comparing such counts, rebuilds its pair state from the input and these bits at every loop, and is trained from answers alone. Each choice removes one way soft attention fails at size: dispersed weight, unresolved gaps between learned scores, and a drifting soft state. In maximum retrieval it is right on at least 99.95% of sets 1,000 times larger than in training, on all ten seeds; trained with a soft count, the same network falls to 42% at 4,096 items. On CLRS-30 without hints, a general form of the layer (half its channels read at zero temperature, numbers embedded, state carried) beats the best published model, which uses hints on some tasks; the full cold layer is exact on every test input of 9 of the 12 tasks whose answers depend on numbers only through comparisons. From yes-or-no answers it decides 2-SAT and two-colouring exactly at 500 variables and, as our theory predicts, not parity equations. Beside a frozen 7B language model it chains family relations exactly at 1,000 statements after training on 16, where the model alone falls to 44%; finite checks on the weights prove every block that learned correct at every size, on acyclic contexts and given what the model reads. On CLUTRR it is right on every story of five to ten relations given the graphs, learning the 62 rules exactly; from text, with the model frozen, no hand-written rule and only a small read-in trained, it lifts an open 7B model from 33% to 65%, above every system we found without hand-written rules except frontier reasoning models.
